newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia late palm olein easier, interest thin.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia late palm olein easier, interest thin.

text.p: Indonesian palm olein prices were easier in late trading on Thursday, with a rebound in Malaysia seen helping boost buying interest, traders said.

They said palm olein was quoted at 1,365-70 rupiah/kg in Jakarta, down from 1,370-75 rupiah at the opening, but trades were also heard at 1,360 rupiah. Crude palm oil was last done at 1,175 rupiah/kg at a tender in Medan on Wednesday.

"The turnaround in Malaysia today will see buyers coming back into our market," one trader said. "Buyers had been waiting for direction from there (Malaysia) and we should see some fresh demand coming in tomorrow."
The traders said prices remained under pressure, as some players were selling below the market range.
"There are people selling at 1,360 rupiah/kg for big volumes," one trader said, adding that brokers had offered to buy olein from him at 1,350 rupiah.
"Some players are trying to push down prices, but I don't think they will succeed because of the rebound in Malaysia," another trader said. "I think local prices will pick up."
The trader said he expected some sellers to raise offers by five rupiah when the market reopens on Friday.

Data from Belawan Port showed that the K.M. Pertiwi will leave the North Sumatran port on Friday for Kuala Enok with 1,000 tonnes of coconut oil. The MT Tirta Kencana will leave on Thursday for Cirebon with 1,800 tonnes of palm olein.
The KM Pershing will leave for Tanjung Priok in Jakarta on Thursday with 4,600 tonnes of coconut oil. The MT Tirta Gama will leave on Thursday for Cilacap with 1,900 tonnes of olein.
